messages.author: 501049b604aa02f8
messages.subject: conditional shading
parts:
Dear friends - I have a very simple question on conditional shading in ggplot2 - 
 x <- 1:10
y <- x^2
IND <- x>3&x<7
 df <- data.frame(x,y,IND)
ggplot(data=df,aes(x,y)) + geom_point()
- now how would I get a nice different shading in the background when IND is TRUE?

All best wishes
Troels

messages.author: bfc2eb6b71169017
messages.subject: Re: conditional shading
parts:
What I would do is make a shadow variable and use it as the black background for your points.

library(ggplot2)

x <- 1:10
y <- x^2
IND <- x>3&x<7
df <- data.frame(x,y,IND)

xoffset <- 0.05
yoffset <- -0.25
df$yshadow <- df$xshadow <- NA

df$xshadow[df$IND] <- df$x[df$IND] + xoffset
df$yshadow[df$IND] <- df$y[df$IND] + yoffset

ggplot(data=df,aes(x,y)) +
  geom_point(aes(x = xshadow, y = yshadow), color = "grey50") +
  geom_point(color = "red")

This way you have extra control over the shadow (position, size).

Cheers,
Roman

messages.author: f20966e9bc9cf5c7
messages.subject: Re: SV: conditional shading
parts:
On Fri, 2018-07-20 at 10:50 +0200, Troels Ring wrote:

 x <- 1:10

y <- x^2

IND <- x>3&x<7

 df <- data.frame(x,y,IND)

ggplot(data=df,aes(x,y)) + geom_point()

- now how would I get a nice different shading in the background when IND is TRUE?
It's ugly, but I use the following code to highlight time series based on the dependent variables' characteristics.

library(ggplot2)
x <- 1:10
y <- x^2
IND <- x>3&x<7

IND2 <-  x* as.integer(!IND)
df <- data.frame(x,y,IND2)

vertical_ribbons <- function(d.f, split_col='dtm', span = 86400 * 2, ...) {
    index <- which(abs(diff(as.numeric(d.f[[split_col]]))) > span)
    splits <- findInterval(1:nrow(d.f), index + .1, T)
    dfs <- split(d.f, splits)
    lapply(dfs, function(d)
        geom_ribbon(data = d, aes(x = x, ymin=-Inf, ymax=Inf),
                    ...)
        )
}


vribs <- vertical_ribbons(df, 'IND2', .5, fill="orange", color = "transparent", alpha=.2)

ggplot(data=df,aes(x,y)) + geom_point() + vribs
